title: Rural Coastal Mountain morning check
summary: Run a short sunrise check of people, official alerts, weather, water, power, communications, and access routes before routine work begins.
content: Procedure: Confirm every expected person and note anyone away, isolated, or needing assistance. Check official civil-protection alerts, weather, wind, sea state, fire conditions, and visible slope or drainage changes. Verify drinking water, essential power, one communication method, and the safest usable route out of the area. Write the single highest-priority correction, assign a responsible person, and set the next review time. Safety limits: Do not enter a closed road, unstable slope, smoke-filled zone, flooded crossing, or rough shoreline merely to complete the check. A quiet morning does not cancel an official warning or remove the need for a backup route.
materials: Printed local map with safe high ground and road alternatives
Battery radio or charged phone reserved for official alerts
One-page status sheet and pencil kept in a dry sleeve
steps: Confirm every expected person and note anyone away, isolated, or needing assistance.
warnings: Do not enter a closed road, unstable slope, smoke-filled zone, flooded crossing, or rough shoreline merely to complete the check.
failure_signs: An expected person cannot be contacted or located.
No verified route, safe water source, or communication method remains available.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain evening review
summary: Close the day with a written review of people, weather changes, supplies used, unfinished hazards, charging, and the overnight watch plan.
content: Procedure: Account for all people and record the location of anyone staying elsewhere overnight. Compare the morning status with current wind, rain, heat, sea, fire, road, and utility conditions. Record water, food, fuel, battery, and medicine use; move tomorrow’s critical items to an accessible dry place. Assign any overnight check, define what will wake the group, and state the first action for the morning. Safety limits: Do not leave fuel-burning equipment, candles, chargers, or damaged batteries operating unattended overnight. Fatigue can hide worsening conditions; use a second person to review critical entries.
steps: Account for all people and record the location of anyone staying elsewhere overnight.
warnings: Do not leave fuel-burning equipment, candles, chargers, or damaged batteries operating unattended overnight.
failure_signs: The overnight responsible person, alarm trigger, or backup light is not confirmed.
A worsening hazard is recorded without a matching action or departure decision.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain priority list
summary: Build one visible priority list that protects life first, then communication, safe water, shelter, medicine, food, sanitation, and recovery work.
content: Procedure: List only unresolved needs and identify which could injure someone within the next hour. Rank life safety, evacuation, communication, water, shelter, medicine, food, sanitation, and property in that order unless official instructions require otherwise. Give each top item one owner, one deadline, and one clear completion test. Cross out completed work, move blocked work to a separate column, and rebuild the list at each major change. Safety limits: Do not let property protection outrank evacuation, medical danger, or safe water. A long list without owners and deadlines is not an operational plan.
materials: Current people, hazard, and supply status
steps: List only unresolved needs and identify which could injure someone within the next hour.
warnings: Do not let property protection outrank evacuation, medical danger, or safe water.
failure_signs: Two critical items compete for the same person or resource with no decision.
The list is older than the latest official alert or major condition change.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain rotation schedule
summary: Rotate demanding tasks so observation, communication, water handling, cooking, care, and rest continue without exhausting one person.
content: Procedure: List essential recurring tasks and the minimum skill or physical ability each requires. Use short shifts for heat, cold, smoke, night watch, heavy carrying, or stressful communication. Pair inexperienced or vulnerable members with suitable support and protect uninterrupted rest periods. At every handover, state current conditions, unfinished work, equipment location, and the exact trigger for escalation. Safety limits: Do not assign a person to a task that conflicts with medication, mobility, hearing, vision, age, or fatigue limits. Continuous work without protected rest increases mistakes and injuries.
materials: Shift board with names and times
steps: List essential recurring tasks and the minimum skill or physical ability each requires.
warnings: Do not assign a person to a task that conflicts with medication, mobility, hearing, vision, age, or fatigue limits.
failure_signs: A shift has no named replacement or handover time.
The same person repeatedly misses rest, meals, medicine, or hydration.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain red label rule
summary: Use a red label to isolate an unsafe room, route, container, tool, food, water source, or electrical item until a competent review clears it.
content: Procedure: Stop use and prevent casual access without touching or moving the hazard unnecessarily. Write the hazard, date, time, reporter, affected area, and required qualified reviewer on the tag. Copy the same information into the isolation log and tell every shift or household member. Remove the label only after the named condition is corrected and the clearance is recorded. Safety limits: A red label warns and isolates; it does not repair electricity, gas, structure, contamination, or spoiled food. Do not place a tag where doing so exposes you to live power, gas, smoke, unstable debris, or contaminated water.
materials: Red tape or durable red tags
steps: Stop use and prevent casual access without touching or moving the hazard unnecessarily.
warnings: A red label warns and isolates; it does not repair electricity, gas, structure, contamination, or spoiled food.
failure_signs: People continue using the marked item or route.
The label lacks a reason, time, or responsible reviewer.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain two-person check
summary: Require two people for consequential checks so one observes the hazard while the other verifies, records, communicates, and can call for help.
content: Procedure: Define the exact check, boundary, and reason two people are required before approaching. Assign one observer and one recorder/communicator; both must understand the stop signal. Maintain line of sight or reliable contact and never allow both people to enter the same hazard zone. Compare observations, record disagreement, and choose the safer interpretation until qualified review. Safety limits: Two untrained people do not make live electrical, gas, structural, cliff, surf, flood, or fire entry safe. Never use the second person as a reason to exceed an official closure or evacuation order.
steps: Define the exact check, boundary, and reason two people are required before approaching.
warnings: Two untrained people do not make live electrical, gas, structural, cliff, surf, flood, or fire entry safe.
failure_signs: Contact between the two people is lost.
Roles, stop signal, or outside help route are unclear.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain quiet-hour plan
summary: Create a protected quiet period for sleep, concentration, children, older adults, and sensory needs while keeping essential watch and alerts active.
content: Procedure: Choose a period based on heat, work shifts, children, medication, and the need for restorative sleep. Move conversations, charging, repairs, and food preparation away from the rest area where practical. Keep one alert receiver and responsible person active, with a visual or vibration method for people who need it. End quiet time immediately for an official warning, missing person, fire, gas, flooding, medical danger, or evacuation. Safety limits: Quiet hours must not silence smoke, carbon-monoxide, weather, evacuation, or medical alarms. Do not leave a single exhausted person responsible for overnight watch.
steps: Choose a period based on heat, work shifts, children, medication, and the need for restorative sleep.
warnings: Quiet hours must not silence smoke, carbon-monoxide, weather, evacuation, or medical alarms.
failure_signs: Essential alerts cannot be heard, seen, or felt in the rest area.
Noise and light continue to prevent vulnerable members from sleeping.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain fallback route
summary: Prepare and verify a fallback route that avoids the same fire, flood, landslide, coastal, snow, or road-closure exposure as the primary route.
content: Procedure: Mark destination, safe high ground, assembly points, fuel limits, walking alternatives, and places that may become choke points. Check whether both routes cross the same bridge, gorge, forest edge, drainage channel, cliff road, or low coastal section. Verify the fallback in safe conditions without entering closures and record travel time for vehicle and foot movement. Write objective triggers for switching early, then share the map with every driver and household member. Safety limits: Never cross moving floodwater, a closed road, active fire area, avalanche zone, rockfall, or dangerous surf to test a route. A route stored only on one phone may disappear with power, damage, or network loss.
materials: Paper map with primary and fallback routes
steps: Mark destination, safe high ground, assembly points, fuel limits, walking alternatives, and places that may become choke points.
warnings: Never cross moving floodwater, a closed road, active fire area, avalanche zone, rockfall, or dangerous surf to test a route.
failure_signs: Primary and fallback routes share the same single failure point.
No one can state the switch trigger or destination without the phone.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain small-kit setup
summary: Build a compact kit for one day of safe movement between village, coast, and mountain conditions without making it too heavy to carry.
content: Procedure: Choose the user and realistic route first; account for age, mobility, heat, cold, salt spray, rain, and steep ground. Pack safe water, simple food, prescribed medicines, basic first aid, light, whistle, map, charging cable, and a weather layer. Place urgent items where they can be reached without unpacking and protect paper and electronics from water. Walk briefly with the loaded kit, remove nonessential weight, and review expiry dates and batteries monthly. Safety limits: Do not include unprescribed medicines, leaking batteries, loose fuel, unknown chemicals, or food that spoils in vehicle heat. A kit does not justify delaying evacuation or entering hazardous terrain.
materials: Water, weather layer, light, whistle, paper map, and power bank
Personal medicine list, identification copy, and emergency contacts
steps: Choose the user and realistic route first; account for age, mobility, heat, cold, salt spray, rain, and steep ground.
warnings: Do not include unprescribed medicines, leaking batteries, loose fuel, unknown chemicals, or food that spoils in vehicle heat.
failure_signs: The intended user cannot carry or open the kit.
Water, medicine, light, map, or emergency contacts are missing or expired.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain clean-dirty boundary
summary: Separate clean living and food areas from mud, saltwater, smoke residue, waste, wet gear, and cleanup tools to limit contamination.
content: Procedure: Choose an entry point and place the dirty zone downwind and downhill where it cannot drain toward food or drinking water. Remove wet or contaminated outer items at the boundary and store them in labelled containers. Wash hands before entering the clean zone and keep food, medicine, bedding, children, and animals away from cleanup waste. Move the boundary when wind, rain, drainage, or work location changes and record contaminated items needing disposal or professional cleaning. Safety limits: Do not mix cleaning chemicals, dry-sweep hazardous dust, or carry contaminated water through the clean zone. Floodwater, sewage, ash, mould, fuel, and unknown powders may require professional controls.
materials: Separate containers for clean and dirty equipment
Handwashing supplies and protective equipment appropriate to the hazard
steps: Choose an entry point and place the dirty zone downwind and downhill where it cannot drain toward food or drinking water.
warnings: Do not mix cleaning chemicals, dry-sweep hazardous dust, or carry contaminated water through the clean zone.
failure_signs: Dirty footwear, tools, or waste repeatedly cross into sleeping or food areas.
The boundary receives runoff, smoke, or windblown debris from the contaminated side.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain storage map
summary: Map where water, food, medicine, tools, fuel, documents, keys, and emergency kits are stored so one local hazard cannot remove everything.
content: Procedure: Mark exits, shutoff points, high shelves, cool rooms, locked hazardous storage, and areas exposed to flood, fire, heat, salt, or collapse. List each critical stock with location, quantity, access person, expiry or inspection date, and minimum reserve. Split essential water, light, communication, documents, and medicine support between at least two suitable locations. Give trusted members a paper copy and update it whenever stock moves or access changes. Safety limits: Do not publish the location of medicines, fuel, valuables, personal records, or keys to people without a legitimate need. Fuel, chemicals, batteries, food, and medicines require different storage boundaries.
materials: Dry off-site copy of the map
steps: Mark exits, shutoff points, high shelves, cool rooms, locked hazardous storage, and areas exposed to flood, fire, heat, salt, or collapse.
warnings: Do not publish the location of medicines, fuel, valuables, personal records, or keys to people without a legitimate need.
failure_signs: The map points to moved, expired, inaccessible, or water-damaged stock.
All copies and all critical supplies remain in the same hazard zone.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain handover note
summary: Use a short handover note so the next person knows current conditions, completed work, unresolved risks, resource levels, and the next decision time.
content: Procedure: Write date, time, outgoing and incoming names, location, and the official alert currently in force. Record people accounted for, urgent support needs, completed actions, active hazards, and isolated items or areas. State water, power, communications, medicine, transport, and staffing limits using measured or clearly labelled estimates. Read the note aloud, let the incoming person ask questions, and sign the exact next check or escalation time. Safety limits: Do not hide uncertainty, injury, missing stock, disagreement, or a missed task to make the shift look successful. Personal medical or identity details should be limited to what the receiver genuinely needs.
steps: Write date, time, outgoing and incoming names, location, and the official alert currently in force.
warnings: Do not hide uncertainty, injury, missing stock, disagreement, or a missed task to make the shift look successful.
failure_signs: The incoming person cannot repeat the top hazard and next action.
The note has no time, responsible name, or next review trigger.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain risk stop rule
summary: Define objective conditions that stop work and trigger shelter, evacuation, professional help, or a new plan before pressure leads to unsafe continuation.
content: Procedure: List local hazards such as visible flame, dense smoke, rising water, rockfall, unstable walls, extreme heat, dangerous surf, lost contact, or medical deterioration. For each hazard, write one observable stop trigger and the immediate safe action. Give every member authority to call the stop without punishment and require a verbal acknowledgement. Resume only after the hazard is controlled, official restrictions allow it, and a new check is documented. Safety limits: A deadline, sunk cost, property concern, or senior person’s preference does not override a stop trigger. Do not invent measurements or claim a hazard is controlled when it has not been verified.
steps: List local hazards such as visible flame, dense smoke, rising water, rockfall, unstable walls, extreme heat, dangerous surf, lost contact, or medical deterioration.
warnings: A deadline, sunk cost, property concern, or senior person’s preference does not override a stop trigger.
failure_signs: Members cannot name the stop signal or immediate safe action.
Work continues after the written trigger occurs.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain training card
summary: Turn one essential local task into a short training card with purpose, prerequisites, steps, stop rules, teach-back, and a review date.
content: Procedure: Choose one bounded task, state who may perform it, and list prerequisites that cannot be learned from the card alone. Write three to seven observable steps in the order used locally, with a picture or landmark when language may fail. Add explicit stop conditions, prohibited shortcuts, and the qualified contact for faults outside the learner’s role. Have the learner explain and demonstrate the task safely; record reviewer, date, and next refresher. Safety limits: A card cannot qualify someone for live electrical, gas, structural, medical, rescue, chainsaw, climbing, boat, or hazardous-chemical work. Do not train with real exposure when a safe simulation is available.
steps: Choose one bounded task, state who may perform it, and list prerequisites that cannot be learned from the card alone.
warnings: A card cannot qualify someone for live electrical, gas, structural, medical, rescue, chainsaw, climbing, boat, or hazardous-chemical work.
failure_signs: The learner cannot explain the stop rule or perform the safe sequence.
The card no longer matches local equipment, route, contact, or official guidance.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain resource ledger
summary: Maintain a transparent ledger of critical supplies received, stored, issued, damaged, reserved, and remaining across dispersed rural, coastal, or mountain locations.
content: Procedure: Define one counting unit for each item and record opening stock by location. For every receipt or issue, write date, quantity, source or recipient, purpose, recorder, and remaining balance. Separate usable, reserved, expired, damaged, contaminated, and unverified stock instead of combining totals. Reconcile physical counts on a schedule, investigate differences, and publish only non-sensitive totals needed for fair planning. Safety limits: Do not alter old entries silently; correct them with a dated line that preserves the audit trail. Do not publish household identities, medicine details, key locations, or security-sensitive stock positions.
materials: Two-person count sheet for high-value stock
steps: Define one counting unit for each item and record opening stock by location.
warnings: Do not alter old entries silently; correct them with a dated line that preserves the audit trail.
failure_signs: The written balance differs from the physical count without explanation.
Stock is issued without date, quantity, purpose, or responsible recorder.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain privacy note
summary: Limit personal information in rural, coastal, or mountain emergency records to what is necessary for safety, access, continuity, and lawful handover.
content: Procedure: For each field, state why it is needed, who may see it, how long it is kept, and what happens when the need ends. Use contact or support codes instead of unnecessary diagnoses, identity numbers, addresses, or family details. Separate public status boards from restricted medical, identity, location, and safeguarding records. Record consent or lawful emergency basis, log access, and securely destroy extra copies when continuity no longer requires them. Safety limits: Never post full names, medical details, live locations, keys, evacuation absences, or identity documents on a public board or open group. Emergency pressure does not justify collecting information that has no safety or continuity purpose.
materials: Privacy note attached to each form
steps: For each field, state why it is needed, who may see it, how long it is kept, and what happens when the need ends.
warnings: Never post full names, medical details, live locations, keys, evacuation absences, or identity documents on a public board or open group.
failure_signs: People cannot learn who has accessed their restricted information.
Public copies contain more personal detail than the action requires.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain low-power habit
summary: Use a scheduled low-power routine that preserves batteries for official alerts, essential communication, medical support, navigation, and safe lighting.
content: Procedure: List devices by life safety, medicine, official alerts, coordination, navigation, lighting, work, and convenience. Set brief communication and charging windows; keep one device powered down as a reserve where practical. Disable nonessential radios, brightness, background data, and repeated searching when no signal exists. Record battery levels and expected runtime, then reallocate power before a critical device reaches its minimum reserve. Safety limits: Do not charge swollen, leaking, overheated, punctured, wet, or otherwise damaged batteries. Never run a generator, charcoal device, or fuel-burning charger indoors or near openings.
steps: List devices by life safety, medicine, official alerts, coordination, navigation, lighting, work, and convenience.
warnings: Do not charge swollen, leaking, overheated, punctured, wet, or otherwise damaged batteries.
failure_signs: A critical communication or medical-support device reaches reserve level with no charged alternative.
Charging demand exceeds safe available power and no priority decision is recorded.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain child-safe version
summary: Adapt local emergency routines so children receive simple roles, clear physical boundaries, identity support, calm explanations, and reliable reunification.
content: Procedure: Assign each child a known adult and a backup; practise the nearby and out-of-area meeting points. Explain the current action in short truthful sentences and give one safe task such as carrying a light item or checking a card. Mark no-go areas around roads, cliffs, water, machinery, cleanup zones, fuel, fire, and unstable ground. Count children at every movement and handover, record who released and received them, and preserve sleep, food, water, medicine, and comfort routines. Safety limits: Never give children watch, fire, fuel, electrical, water-crossing, cliff, vehicle-control, or hazardous-cleanup duties. Do not publish a child’s full identity, live location, or absence to an open channel.
materials: Child contact card without unnecessary private detail
steps: Assign each child a known adult and a backup; practise the nearby and out-of-area meeting points.
warnings: Never give children watch, fire, fuel, electrical, water-crossing, cliff, vehicle-control, or hazardous-cleanup duties.
failure_signs: A child is moved without a named receiving adult or written count.
The child cannot state or show the safe meeting point appropriate to their age.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain elder support version
summary: Adapt village, coast, and mountain continuity plans for older adults by linking check-ins, medicine records, mobility, hearing, heat, cold, and transport support.
content: Procedure: Ask the person what help they want and record communication, mobility, medicine, continence, food, temperature, and device needs. Set check-in times and a missed-check trigger, with a nearby helper and a backup who can access the home lawfully. Prepare safe transport for stairs, rough ground, heat, cold, ferry or road interruption without lifting methods beyond training. At every move, transfer the medicine list, mobility aids, glasses, hearing supplies, identification, contacts, water, and destination. Safety limits: Do not change prescribed doses, force assistance, remove decision-making, or use unsafe manual lifting. Heat, cold, dehydration, infection, confusion, falls, breathing difficulty, and missed medicine may require prompt professional assessment.
materials: Mobility aid, spare sensory-device supplies, and transport plan
steps: Ask the person what help they want and record communication, mobility, medicine, continence, food, temperature, and device needs.
warnings: Do not change prescribed doses, force assistance, remove decision-making, or use unsafe manual lifting.
failure_signs: A scheduled check-in is missed and no backup confirms safety.
Transport, medicine, mobility aid, or communication support is unavailable when conditions worsen.

title: Rural Coastal Mountain Greek-English sign
summary: Post a concise Greek-English emergency sign that states the verified hazard, affected area, required action, direction, source, time, and next update.
content: Procedure: Write the action first in Greek and English using short verbs such as leave, do not enter, boil water, shelter, or meeting point. Add the exact affected place, safe direction or destination, date and time, official source, and next expected update. Use large letters, high contrast, arrows, and a simple symbol; place copies at decision points without blocking exits. Have one Greek reader and one English reader independently explain the sign, then replace it when the instruction changes or expires. Safety limits: Do not invent authority, translate uncertain information as fact, or leave an expired instruction displayed. Avoid names, medical details, live household locations, or other private information on a public sign.
materials: Thick dark marker and directional arrows
steps: Write the action first in Greek and English using short verbs such as leave, do not enter, boil water, shelter, or meeting point.
warnings: Do not invent authority, translate uncertain information as fact, or leave an expired instruction displayed.
failure_signs: Greek and English readers understand different actions or destinations.
The sign has no time, source, affected area, or next-update point.
